events.extended_summary: The General Medical Council (GMC) has apologised after erroneously emailing personal identifiable data relating to 223 doctors to a newspaper. The information, sent in error when responding to a media request, included GMC unique identification numbers, details of allegations of antisemitism or Islamophobia, and in some cases ethnicity. Some complaints did not meet the threshold for investigation, meaning affected doctors may have learned of allegations for the first time through the breach notification. The newspaper has stated it will not publish the private details at this stage but will not delete the data. The GMC has contacted affected doctors to apologise and offer support, and has reported itself to the Information Commissioner's Office. The British Medical Association condemned the breach as unacceptable, noting doctors are entitled to confidentiality, while the Doctors' Association UK called for an independent investigation into how the leak occurred and demanded the information be deleted.
events.micro_summary: The GMC erroneously shared personal data of 223 doctors with a newspaper.
events.summary: The General Medical Council apologised after erroneously emailing personal identifiable data of 223 doctors, including complaint details and ethnicity, to a newspaper, which has refused to delete the information despite promising not to publish it.

events.extended_summary: Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge across the Kerch Strait again on Wednesday, temporarily halting traffic two days after a previous strike destroyed a 227-metre section of the road span. The Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea confirmed the latest attack, stating that damage assessment is underway and all relevant services are on site. This marks the third strike on the bridge this week. The 19-kilometre bridge, which links annexed Crimea to Russia's Krasnodar Krai and is the longest in Europe, was previously hit in October 2022 and July 2023. While the road section collapsed in the earlier attack, the railway corridor remains operational despite sustaining damage. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the earlier operation as unprecedented, involving domestically produced Palianytsia drones and Neptune missiles. Russia has vowed to restore the bridge, though experts estimate repairs could take a year or more.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge again, halting traffic after a 227-metre road section was destroyed.
events.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Crimean Bridge for the third time this week, temporarily halting traffic after a previous attack destroyed a 227-metre road section while the rail line remains operational.

events.extended_summary: Donald Trump will meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of a summit for Asia-Pacific countries. The trilateral meeting, reportedly proposed by Putin, comes as Trump appears to embrace a reorientation of American foreign policy toward spheres of influence. While Trump has expressed interest in discussing nuclear disarmament, substantive discussion of artificial intelligence is not expected. The gathering has unsettled traditional US allies, with Eastern European leaders including Volodymyr Zelensky and Poland's foreign minister Radosław Sikorski warning against a reprise of the 1945 Yalta Conference. However, analysts argue comparisons are overblown as no agenda has been agreed in advance. The meeting occurs alongside Quad naval exercises in the Western Pacific involving US, Japanese, Australian, and Indian forces, highlighting shifting geopolitical alignments.
events.micro_summary: Donald Trump meets Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen for a trilateral summit on Thursday.
events.summary: Donald Trump meets Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of an Asia-Pacific summit, with nuclear disarmament among possible topics.

events.extended_summary: Israeli forces launched a ground operation in central Gaza, advancing west of the Yellow Line marking the area under Israeli control under the October 10, 2025 ceasefire. The operation, the first major ground offensive since the ceasefire took effect, targeted areas near the Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps, with tanks and bulldozers advancing toward Salah al-Din Street amid heavy gunfire and artillery. The military issued evacuation orders and closed a section of the road, stating the precise operation aimed to dismantle a terror tunnel and remove threats. Hamas accused Israel of a flagrant violation of the ceasefire. Attacks killed four Palestinians: one in al-Mughraqa and three in Deir el-Balah, Nuseirat and Gaza City. The Yellow Line now encompasses around two-thirds of Gaza, where more than two million Palestinians live in the remaining territory, mostly in tents. The US-backed Board of Peace had warned the 13-month-old agreement risks collapse.
events.micro_summary: Israeli forces launched a ground operation in central Gaza west of the ceasefire line, killing four people.
events.summary: Israeli forces launched a ground operation in central Gaza west of the Yellow Line ceasefire boundary, advancing toward Salah al-Din Street near Nuseirat and Bureij camps, issuing evacuation orders, and killing four Palestinians in attacks.

events.extended_summary: Israel postponed issuing contracts for the E1 West Bank settlement days after the UK sanctioned eight building firms operating in the area. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu should not decide on expansion, ordering the Israel land authority and housing ministry not to open the tender for 3,401 housing units. The land between Jerusalem and Ma'aleh Adumim bisects the West Bank and cuts it off from East Jerusalem. Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not a response to UK measures, while UK diplomats believe growing political pressure is having an impact. Gadi Eisenkot, seen as Israel's most likely next prime minister, opposed the expansion as a mistake likely to alienate international opinion.
events.micro_summary: Israel postponed the E1 settlement tender for 3,401 housing units after the attorney general barred the caretaker government from deciding.
events.summary: Israel postponed issuing contracts for the E1 West Bank settlement, with the attorney general ordering the caretaker government not to open the tender for 3,401 housing units, days after the UK sanctioned eight construction firms operating in the area.

events.extended_summary: Demographic projections estimate future changes in the size and geographic distribution of seven religious groups—Christians, Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists, Jews, followers of other religions, and the religiously unaffiliated—between 2020 and 2070. The analysis covers 201 countries and territories representing 99.98% of the world's population. Researchers employed an advanced cohort-based method, projecting populations by age and sex groups while modeling births, deaths, immigration, and emigration. The model incorporates differences in fertility rates between religious groups, past patterns of religious switching, and data from national censuses, surveys, 2024 global population prospects, and migration flow estimates. The projections establish 2020 as the baseline year and do not account for potential disruptions such as wars, natural disasters, or epidemics.
events.micro_summary: Projections forecast changes in seven religious groups' global populations through 2070 across 201 countries.
events.summary: Demographic projections estimate the size and distribution of seven religious groups from 2020 to 2070 across 201 countries covering 99.98% of the world's population, incorporating fertility, mortality, migration, and religious switching data.

events.extended_summary: In the past week, technology outages disrupted US services. A Microsoft network upgrade caused server overload, while a Federal Aviation Administration failure involving a copper wire upgrade and outdated equipment grounded all US flights for more than four hours, longest halt since September 11, 2001. The National Security Agency had communication problems, Apple's iCloud and Apple Pay suffered disruptions, JPMorgan Chase reported a software bug affecting banks, and a United Airlines failure delayed about 150 flights. Separately, AI discovered flaws in Java, and malicious code in Optimizely allowed hackers to steal approximately $7,000 in cryptocurrency. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated there was zero evidence linking incidents or indicating a systemic attack, asserting they were not inter-related and not caused by cyber-criminals or hostile actors. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton confirmed outages were not a cyber-attack, explaining institutions were patching or upgrading systems, causing disruptions.
events.micro_summary: Recent major tech outages affecting Microsoft, US flights, banks and Apple were unrelated and not cyber-attacks, officials say.
events.summary: Major tech outages grounded all US flights for over four hours and disrupted Microsoft, Apple, banks and the NSA, but officials state there is zero evidence linking them or indicating a cyber-attack, blaming outdated infrastructure and failed updates.

events.extended_summary: US Central Command has expanded its military operations in the Middle East through multiple initiatives. On November 7, the command announced Task Force Iron Gate, a 20-member team based in Tampa, Florida, designed to disrupt the movement of weapons and sanctioned materials across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea, complementing the existing naval blockade that has prevented over $25 billion in Iranian exports. Meanwhile, Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper is expected to arrive in Saudi Arabia this week with more than three dozen military advisors to examine the kingdom's air defense capabilities. The visit comes as Saudi Arabia faces Houthi aerial attacks, including four strikes on Riyadh airport within one week last month that killed at least 13 people, amid concerns about the kingdom's vulnerability to drone attacks.
events.micro_summary: US launches 20-member Task Force Iron Gate against Iran and sends advisors to Saudi Arabia.
events.summary: US Central Command announced Task Force Iron Gate, a 20-member team targeting Iran's land routes, while sending over three dozen advisors to Saudi Arabia to examine air defenses amid Houthi attacks.

events.extended_summary: Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a shock exit from the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton after losing 10-8 to 16th seed Jermaine Wattimena in the second round. The 19-year-old world champion had earlier hit a remarkable 150 checkout by landing three bullseyes against Niels Zonneveld to secure his place in the last 16, though he lost that group match 5-4. Wattimena, 38, hit 10 maximum 180s and averaged 101.70 to secure the victory, while Littler averaged 101.38. The Dutchman twice threatened nine-darters and progressed to the quarter-finals where he will face compatriot Kevin Doets. Littler had asked the crowd whether he should attempt the audacious finish before throwing the three darts.
events.micro_summary: Defending champion Luke Littler lost 10-8 to Jermaine Wattimena, ending his Grand Slam of Darts title defense.
events.summary: Luke Littler's title defense ended at the Grand Slam of Darts with a 10-8 second-round defeat to Jermaine Wattimena after he had hit a 150 checkout against Niels Zonneveld.

events.extended_summary: Richmond's line-ball call on its second selection is poised to shape the top of the 2026 AFL Draft's uncertain first round. The Tigers met on Tuesday to decide between ruckman Harry Van Hattum and powerful forward Gus Teixeira for the No.8 pick, with rivals believing the club will settle on Van Hattum as the favourite. Recruiting boss Rhy Gieschen described the Northern Knights prospect as one of the best ruck talents of the past decade. Should Richmond select Van Hattum, Teixeira could land at Sydney, Gold Coast, St Kilda, Adelaide or Melbourne depending on how the first round unfolds. Sydney is also linked to West Australian midfielder Leo Steed, Sam Gayfer, Clancy Snell and Tyson Bradley. Clubs anticipate a highly unpredictable second half of the first round with potential order swings involving Richmond, Sydney and Collingwood.
events.micro_summary: Richmond is expected to select Harry Van Hattum with its No.8 pick in the 2026 AFL Draft.
events.summary: Richmond's decision between ruckman Harry Van Hattum and forward Gus Teixeira for its No.8 selection is expected to shape the top of the 2026 AFL Draft, with rivals believing the Tigers will choose Van Hattum.

events.extended_summary: With two weeks remaining before the sport is expected to shut down, Commissioner Rob Manfred said Wednesday that MLB was prepared to go to war over its proposed salary cap. The commissioner stated that the league was ready to fight for the salary cap system. The players, however, have long said they will not accept the proposed salary cap. The statement comes as MLB faces a shutdown in two weeks, with the league prepared to go to war over the issue while the players remain opposed to the system they have long rejected. The dispute centers on the salary cap proposal that the players have long said they will not accept.
events.micro_summary: Commissioner Rob Manfred says MLB is prepared to go to war over a salary cap with two weeks until shutdown.
events.summary: MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said Wednesday that the league is prepared to go to war over its proposed salary cap, which players have long rejected, with two weeks remaining before the sport is expected to shut down.

events.extended_summary: Democrats in the US House nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first Black lawmaker to lead the chamber. The House will elect its new Speaker on January 3, when Democrats will hold the majority. Jeffries was re-elected as party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on Wednesday. Democrats will hold at least 257 seats next year, beyond the 218 needed for a majority, with seven races still uncalled. Jeffries, who represents a New York district, has served as minority leader since 2023. Seven incoming lawmakers from the party's left wing stated that more work is needed to reflect constituent demands. President Donald Trump has signalled willingness to work with Democrats on some issues but pledged to veto legislation he opposes.
events.micro_summary: Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries as Speaker, positioning him to become the first Black lawmaker to lead the House.
events.summary: House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first Black lawmaker to lead the chamber when the new term begins on January 3.

events.extended_summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran stated that India expects stronger growth and improved capital flows in 2027-28 as four headwinds ease, including US relations, energy markets, absence of an 'AI play', and higher developed-world interest rates. He noted AI capital flowing in reverse will help attract FDI, citing $5 billion in inflows over two months during AI concerns. The rupee, which hit 96.88 against the dollar on October 8, rebounded to 93.41, and he suggested next year's challenge may be managing rupee strength rather than weakness. Exports reached $568.8 billion in the first seven months, up 16.7%, and are projected to approach $1 trillion by March 2027, while imports totaled $662.2 billion, up 16%. India recorded 7.8% growth in the first quarter, with manufacturing expanding 9.2%, and faces dual tailwinds from crude oil and the AI bubble.
events.micro_summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran predicts India's exports will hit $1 trillion by March 2027.
events.summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran said exports reached $568 billion in seven months, likely hitting $1 trillion by March 2027, and predicted stronger growth in 2027-28 as the rupee rebounded to 93.41.

events.extended_summary: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh launched the curtain raiser for the 12th India International Science Festival (IISF) 2026 at the National Media Centre in New Delhi. The four-day festival will be held in Pune from December 19 to 22 under the theme 'India's Science, World's Future.' Singh unveiled the official website and brochure, urging the scientific community to take research beyond laboratories and connect with young people, startups, entrepreneurs and society. He said IISF 2026 reflects Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of Vishwa Bandhu Bharat and India's growing global scientific role, citing indigenous research kits developed by the Department of Biotechnology and carried to the International Space Station by astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla. Singh noted that as India advances toward Viksit Bharat 2047, its scientific capabilities will shape the global research ecosystem. IISF serves as a public-facing platform with international participation, distinct from the academic-focused Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave.
events.micro_summary: Union Minister Jitendra Singh launched the curtain raiser for the 12th India International Science Festival 2026 in New Delhi.
events.summary: Union Minister Jitendra Singh launched the curtain raiser for the 12th India International Science Festival 2026 in New Delhi, unveiling the website and brochure for the Pune festival scheduled December 19-22 under the theme 'India's Science, World's Future'.

events.extended_summary: Hitachi Systems India has launched an Advanced Global Delivery Centre in Bengaluru in partnership with US-based cybersecurity company CrowdStrike. The centre provides AI-powered cybersecurity and managed security services to organisations across India, Asia Pacific and the Middle East, combining Hitachi's systems integration with CrowdStrike's Falcon platform. The initiative addresses security challenges from AI adoption, helping enterprises identify vulnerabilities and strengthen operations. Hitachi Systems India joined CrowdStrike's Project QuiltWorks, which integrates frontier AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic, NVIDIA's Nemotron models, threat intelligence, AWS infrastructure and automated workflows to identify vulnerabilities. The company will offer CrowdStrike's Frontier AI Readiness and Resilience (FAIRR) Service for AI-powered vulnerability scanning and risk prioritisation, plus Falcon Guardian, an AI Detection and Response solution with an AI Kill Switch to terminate rogue agents. The partnership also covers Falcon Next-Gen SIEM services. Target customers include banking, financial services and healthcare enterprises.
events.micro_summary: Hitachi Systems India launched a Bengaluru delivery centre with CrowdStrike to provide AI-powered cybersecurity services.
events.summary: Hitachi Systems India launched an Advanced Global Delivery Centre in Bengaluru with CrowdStrike, offering AI-powered cybersecurity and managed security services to enterprises across India, Asia Pacific and the Middle East using the Falcon platform.

events.extended_summary: The All India Football Federation filed a complaint with the Asian Football Confederation over an alleged racist gesture by Palestinian midfielder Taha Soueidan toward India under-17 captain Dallalmuon Gangte during their AFC U17 Asian Cup 2027 qualifier in Kuala Lumpur, which India won 4-1. Footage showed Soueidan fanning himself near Gangte during first-half stoppage time. The AIFF asked the AFC to review the incident and take action, stating racism has no place in football. Soueidan, 15, who plays for FC Union Berlin's under-17 team, denied the accusation, saying the gesture was due to high humidity, not racism. He said he approached Gangte to assure him he meant no offense. The match also saw Palestinian midfielder Mohammed Jamhour sent off for kicking Indian player Raj Singh Wahengbam twice.
events.micro_summary: AIFF lodges complaint with AFC over alleged racist gesture during India's 4-1 U17 win over Palestine.
events.summary: The All India Football Federation complained to the Asian Football Confederation over an alleged racist gesture by Palestinian midfielder Taha Soueidan toward India captain Dallalmuon Gangte during their AFC U17 qualifier, which India won 4-1 in Kuala Lumpur.
